chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about Tayammum, so he recited this Verse:
And (as for) the man who steals and the woman who steals, cut off their hands
and He said: wash your faces and your hands as far as the elbows
He said: Therefore wipe upon (the back of your) wrists from where is the place of the cut.
And He said: and your Lord was not forgetful
ai.seo_question: How does the Quranic verse on cutting the hands of thieves relate to the Islamic ritual of Tayammum?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the mechanics of Tayammum by drawing a linguistic and legal analogy from Surah Al-Ma'idah, linking the wiping of hands in dry ablution to the cutting of hands in the verse of theft (5:38). This interpretation highlights the precision of divine legislation, reinforced by the concluding verse (19:64) which affirms God's perfect memory and attention to detail in prescribing rituals. The narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that Quranic terms often carry multiple layers of legal implication derived from their contextual usage.
